subtitle: A disruptive brother and the cave episode

disruption.work: Old-World Japan: Old-World Japan, Susanoo's destructive conduct
disruption.author: Frank Rinder
disruption.locator: Old-World Japan, Susanoo's destructive conduct; local text normalized characters 14365-15621
disruption.excerpt: Susa-no-o, the brother of Ama-terasu, who had resigned his ocean sceptre and now reigned as the Moon-God, was jealous of his sister's glory and world-wide sway. The Heaven-Illuminating Spirit had but to whisper and she was heard throughout her kingdom, even in the depths of the clear pool and in the heart of the crystal. Her rice-fields, whether situated on hill-side, in sheltered valley, or by running stream, yielded abundant harvests, and her groves were laden with fruit. But the voice of Susa-no-o was not so clear, his smile was not so radiant. The undulating fields which lay around his palace were now flooded, now parched, and his rice crops were often destroyed. The wrath and jealousy of the Moon-God knew no bounds, yet Ama-terasu was infinitely patient and forgave him many things. Once, as was her wont, the Sun-Goddess sat in the central court of her glorious home. She plied her shuttle. Celestial weaving maidens surrounded a fountain whose waters were fragrant with the heavenly lotus-bloom: they sang softly of the clouds and the wind and the lift of the sky. Suddenly, the body of a piebald horse fell through the vast dome at their feet: the "Beloved of the Gods" had been "flayed with a backward flaying" by the envious Susa-no-o.
disruption.note: Rinder's modern retelling, not a direct Kojiki translation.

withdrawal.excerpt: Ama-terasu, trembling at the horrible sight, pricked her finger with the weaving shuttle, and, profoundly indignant at the cruelty of her brother, withdrew into a cave and closed behind her the door of the Heavenly Rock Dwelling. The universe was plunged in darkness.
withdrawal.note: Rinder's modern retelling, not a direct Kojiki translation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: In Rinder's retelling, Susanoo's actions damage the fields and culminate in violence at Amaterasu's weaving hall. She withdraws into the cave, and darkness spreads.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: This passage makes a family conflict matter beyond the family: Amaterasu's withdrawal changes the world's light. Keep it distinct from other Susanoo episodes and later retellings.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read the source boundary
narrativeBlocks.body: The citation is Rinder's modern compilation of Japanese mythic traditions. It supports claims about this retelling, not every account of Susanoo or all Japanese religious practice.
